name: GuardrailCheck
title: Guardrail Check
description: Check text against an AWS Bedrock guardrail — block, flag or mask content by your organization's policy.
whenToUse: Screen a piece of text against your organization's content policy before acting on it: user submissions before they are stored, scraped pages before they are indexed, generated copy before it is sent. It applies an AWS Bedrock guardrail your security team configured — denied topics, PII rules, content filters — and answers with passed or intervened, plus the text with any masking applied. It checks and transforms text only; it cannot generate content or decide policy itself.

inputs.name: text
inputs.description: The text to check, usually wired from an upstream node's output

outputs.name: passed
outputs.description: true when the guardrail found nothing — the clean-path signal to branch on

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The text to carry forward — the original when it passed, the masked version when the guardrail transformed it

outputs.name: action
outputs.description: The guardrail's verdict verbatim — NONE or GUARDRAIL_INTERVENED

outputs.name: assessments
outputs.description: What tripped and why — per-policy findings for logging or routing

text.title: Text
text.description: The text to check. Usually wired from an upstream node, e.g. return signal.llamaparse1.text

guardrailId.title: Guardrail ID
guardrailId.description: The Bedrock guardrail's identifier from the AWS console (e.g. gr0abcd1234ef). The guardrail lives in the AWS account and region of this node's credential — policy is authored there, this node only applies it.

guardrailVersion.title: Guardrail Version
guardrailVersion.description: A numbered version to pin, or DRAFT for the working copy. Pin a number in production — DRAFT changes under editing.

source.title: Checking As
source.description: Which half of the guardrail's rules apply. INPUT treats the text as something a person or upstream system submitted; OUTPUT treats it as something a model produced. The same guardrail carries different rules for each.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: aws-bedrock
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# BEDROCK AS MANIFESTS, and the cheapest AWS package to convert: both API calls it makes
# (Converse and InvokeModel) are plain signed JSON POSTs. Everything it needed already
# existed by the time it was reached — the signer from DynamoDB, and `transport: binary`
# for the attachments Claude can read.
#
# The retired TypeScript is at `_legacy/nodes/aws-bedrock/`.

name: aws-bedrock
displayName: AWS Bedrock
description: Claude and GPT models plus Titan embeddings on AWS Bedrock
version: 2.1.0
category: ai
publisher: unoverse
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749137717/gravity/icons/vdyfnijyuyk8ajqtp3nu.webp

features:
  - Claude on Bedrock via the native Messages API, with images, documents and tools
  - GPT on Bedrock, one prompt to one completion
  - Titan text embeddings, inline or over a service edge
  - Apply Bedrock guardrails to any text — screen, block or mask by your org's policy

# Two labels deep at least: bedrock-runtime.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com.
allowedHosts:
  - "**.amazonaws.com"
  # The bedrock-mantle endpoint, AWS's host for the native Anthropic Messages API:
  # bedrock-mantle.us-east-1.api.aws.
  - "**.api.aws"
  # Any host, for the UNAUTHENTICATED attachment fetches only. BedrockClaude reads an image
  # or document from a url a person supplies, which cannot be declared in advance. Those
  # calls send no credential, and the executor refuses "*" the moment one does.
  - "*"

requires:
  # SigV4 for the embeddings nodes; the LLM nodes authenticate with a Bedrock API key,
  # x-api-key on the Mantle endpoint and bearer on bedrock-runtime.
  credential: [awsSigV4, apiKeyHeader, bearer]
  transport: [json, binary]
  # Bedrock embeds ONE text per request, so a batch is a fan-out.
  chunk: true
  executorVersion: ">=1.4.0"

credentials.awsCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# Transcribed from plugin-base's shared AWSCredential, NAME AND FIELDS UNCHANGED so
# credentials already stored against `awsCredential` keep resolving. Every AWS package
# shares this one, exactly as they shared the TypeScript definition.
#
# sessionToken is NEW, and additive. The retired definition had no such field, so anyone on
# temporary credentials (an assumed role, anything via STS) could not use these nodes at
# all. The signer sends and signs it only when it is filled in.

name: awsCredential
displayName: AWS Credentials
description: AWS credentials for AWS services (DynamoDB, S3, Bedrock, and the rest)
documentationUrl: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_credentials_access-keys.html

properties:
  - name: accessKeyId
    displayName: Access Key ID
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your AWS Access Key ID
    placeholder: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
  - name: secretAccessKey
    displayName: Secret Access Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your AWS Secret Access Key
    placeholder: ""
  - name: region
    displayName: AWS Region
    type: string
    required: false
    default: us-east-1
    description: The region your tables live in
    placeholder: us-east-1
  - name: sessionToken
    displayName: Session Token
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: true
    description: Only for temporary credentials from STS or an assumed role. Leave empty for a long-lived key.
    placeholder: ""
credentials.bedrockCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

# A Bedrock API key, NOT an IAM access-key pair. Minted on the Bedrock console's API keys
# page, it authenticates as a plain header with no SigV4 signing: `x-api-key` against the
# bedrock-mantle Anthropic endpoint, `Authorization: Bearer` against bedrock-runtime.
#
# The embeddings nodes keep the signed awsCredential; this one belongs to the LLM nodes.

name: bedrockCredential
displayName: AWS Bedrock
description: API key credentials for AWS Bedrock model calls
documentationUrl: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/api-keys.html

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: A Bedrock API key from the Bedrock console
    placeholder: ABSK...

  - name: region
    displayName: Region
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: The AWS region your Bedrock models are enabled in
    placeholder: us-east-1

shared.bedrock.yaml:
# The one call shape every Bedrock node makes.
#
# Bedrock is REST, unlike DynamoDB: the model id is in the PATH and the operation is the
# last segment, so there is no X-Amz-Target header here. `bedrock-runtime` is the signing
# service name and is NOT the same as the console's "bedrock" — signing against the wrong
# one is a 403 that says nothing about which name was wrong.

call: &call
  method: POST
  credential:
    scheme: awsSigV4
    service: bedrock-runtime
  headers:
    Content-Type: application/json
    Accept: application/json
  transport: json
  # Bedrock throttles hard under load and answers 429; retrying is the difference between a
  # workflow that survives a burst and one that fails a step at random.
  retry:
    attempts: 4
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]

host: &host >-
  return 'https://bedrock-runtime.' + (credentials.awsCredential.region || 'us-east-1') + '.amazonaws.com'

# The same call, authenticated with a Bedrock API key instead of request signing.
# bedrock-runtime accepts the key as a plain bearer header, so the executor needs no
# signer for the nodes that use this shape.
keyCall: &keyCall
  method: POST
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.bedrockCredential.apiKey }}"
  headers:
    Content-Type: application/json
    Accept: application/json
  transport: json
  retry:
    attempts: 4
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504]
shared.models.yaml:
# The canonical Bedrock model lists, one per model family, organised by TIER.
#
# Same contract as openai/shared/models.yaml: the data lives here, the fallback logic
# (`resolve: modelTier` on the config field) lives in the executor. A new generation is
# a per-tier edit here, and every node plus every saved workflow moves over automatically.
#
# Bedrock ids carry the vendor prefix. Enable each model for your region in the Bedrock
# console before first use; that is an account setting, not something a manifest can do.

claude:
  # Listed large first so the strongest reads first. The picker's options.
  enum:
    - anthropic.claude-opus-5
    - anthropic.claude-sonnet-5
    - anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5

  # Version numbers in the labels by request. When a generation ships, the label is
  # edited alongside the id, or the two lie together.
  enumNames:
    - Claude Opus 5 (Frontier, complex work)
    - Claude Sonnet 5 (Balanced intelligence/cost)
    - Claude Haiku 4.5 (Cost-optimized, high-volume)

  # Balanced middle tier, the sensible default for most work.
  default: anthropic.claude-sonnet-5

gpt:
  enum:
    - openai.gpt-5.6-sol
    - openai.gpt-5.6-terra
    - openai.gpt-5.6-luna

  enumNames:
    - GPT-5.6 Sol (Frontier, complex work)
    - GPT-5.6 Terra (Balanced intelligence/cost)
    - GPT-5.6 Luna (Cost-optimized, high-volume)

  default: openai.gpt-5.6-terra

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# `response` is ApplyGuardrail's reply: { action, outputs: [{ text }], assessments, usage }.
# `action` is NONE (clean) or GUARDRAIL_INTERVENED (blocked or masked).

- emit: passed
  value: "return response.action === 'NONE'"

- emit: text
  # THE TEXT TO CARRY FORWARD, which is the masked form when the guardrail transformed it —
  # redact-and-proceed is what a document pipeline usually wants, and the caller still has
  # `passed` and `assessments` to branch on when proceeding is wrong. When the guardrail
  # intervened without producing output (a hard block), this is EMPTY, deliberately: carrying
  # the original text past a block would defeat the check.
  value: >-
    return response.action === 'NONE'
      ? String(config.text || '')
      : (((response.outputs || [])[0] || {}).text || '')

- emit: action
  value: "return response.action || ''"

- emit: assessments
  value: "return response.assessments || []"
files.api/run.yaml:
# APPLYGUARDRAIL, the standalone form. Grounded in the Bedrock Runtime API reference: the guardrail
# is named in the PATH, the text and direction travel in the body, and the reply carries the
# verdict, the transformed text when masking applied, and per-policy assessments.
#
#   POST /guardrail/{guardrailIdentifier}/version/{guardrailVersion}/apply
#   body: { source: INPUT | OUTPUT, content: [ { text: { text } } ] }
#
# STANDALONE is the point: this call checks TEXT, not a Bedrock model invocation, so the text can
# come from anywhere — an OpenAI completion, a parsed document, a form submission. It is the same
# API the platform's coming clip-on enforcement will use, proved here first as an ordinary node.

- $ref: bedrock#call
  name: check
  url: >-
    return 'https://bedrock-runtime.' + (credentials.awsCredential.region || 'us-east-1')
      + '.amazonaws.com/guardrail/' + encodeURIComponent(config.guardrailId)
      + '/version/' + encodeURIComponent(config.guardrailVersion || 'DRAFT') + '/apply'
  body:
    source: "{{ config.source }}"
    content: >-
      return [ { text: { text: String(config.text || '') } } ]
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  # `source` is required because the vendor requires it in the body and a blank template drops the
  # key (the droppable-body guard caught exactly this); it has a default, so requiring it costs an
  # author nothing.
  required: [guardrailId, source]
  properties:
    text:
      type: string
      title: Text
      description: >-
        The text to check. Usually wired from an upstream node, e.g. return signal.llamaparse1.text
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    guardrailId:
      type: string
      title: Guardrail ID
      description: >-
        The Bedrock guardrail's identifier from the AWS console (e.g. gr0abcd1234ef). The guardrail
        lives in the AWS account and region of this node's credential — policy is authored there,
        this node only applies it.
      default: ""
    guardrailVersion:
      type: string
      title: Guardrail Version
      # DRAFT is the working copy and the right default for building; production workflows should
      # pin a numbered version so a mid-edit policy never applies itself.
      description: >-
        A numbered version to pin, or DRAFT for the working copy. Pin a number in production —
        DRAFT changes under editing.
      default: DRAFT
    source:
      type: string
      title: Checking As
      description: >-
        Which half of the guardrail's rules apply. INPUT treats the text as something a person or
        upstream system submitted; OUTPUT treats it as something a model produced. The same
        guardrail carries different rules for each.
      enum: [INPUT, OUTPUT]
      enumNames: [Input (submitted content), Output (model-generated content)]
      default: INPUT
"ui:order":
  [text, guardrailId, guardrailVersion, source]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: text
    type: string
    description: The text to check, usually wired from an upstream node's output
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: passed
    type: boolean
    description: true when the guardrail found nothing — the clean-path signal to branch on
  - name: text
    type: string
    description: The text to carry forward — the original when it passed, the masked version when the guardrail transformed it
  - name: action
    type: string
    description: The guardrail's verdict verbatim — NONE or GUARDRAIL_INTERVENED
  - name: assessments
    type: array
    description: What tripped and why — per-policy findings for logging or routing

credentials:
  - name: awsCredential
    required: true
    displayName: AWS
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: GuardrailCheck
kind: PromiseNode

name: Guardrail Check
category: Documents
color: "#01A88D"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749137717/gravity/icons/vdyfnijyuyk8ajqtp3nu.webp

description: Check text against an AWS Bedrock guardrail — block, flag or mask content by your organization's policy.

# THE EXPLICIT VERB, not the safety net. The platform-level clip-on guardrail (the per-box policy
# the executor enforces) is a separate, coming capability that will reuse this node's proven wire
# format. This node exists for workflows where checking IS the step: moderate an upload before
# storing it, screen scraped content before indexing, gate a user submission.
#
# Outcome first, then disqualify by PROPERTY (doc 14): never name another node.
whenToUse: >-
  Screen a piece of text against your organization's content policy before acting on it: user
  submissions before they are stored, scraped pages before they are indexed, generated copy before
  it is sent. It applies an AWS Bedrock guardrail your security team configured — denied topics,
  PII rules, content filters — and answers with passed or intervened, plus the text with any
  masking applied. It checks and transforms text only; it cannot generate content or decide policy
  itself.

auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # The same text against the same guardrail VERSION is deterministic, but DRAFT guardrails
  # change under editing and a cached "passed" outliving a policy tightening is the worst
  # possible staleness.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# Running it live needs AWS credentials AND a guardrail that exists in that account — there is no
# public fixture guardrail, so guardrailId below must be EDITED to a real one before running (any
# content policy will do; the id is on the guardrail's console page). Benign text, so the fixture
# asserts the CLEAN path: action NONE, passed true, text carried through unchanged. The intervened
# path is exercised by pointing the same node at text the guardrail's own policy rejects.

testData:
  config:
    text: The quarterly report is attached. Please review the revenue figures on page three.
    guardrailId: EDIT-ME-your-guardrail-id
    guardrailVersion: DRAFT
    source: INPUT
  inputs: {}
  expect:
    passed: "return output.passed === true"
    text: "return typeof output.text === 'string' && output.text.length > 0"
    action: "return output.action === 'NONE'"
    assessments: "return Array.isArray(output.assessments)"
